categories.main_business_segments: CarMax operates in two reportable segments: CarMax Sales Operations and CarMax Auto Finance (CAF). The Sales Operations segment includes all aspects of auto merchandising and service operations, such as retail and wholesale vehicle sales, extended protection plans, and vehicle repair services. The CAF segment provides vehicle financing to customers purchasing retail vehicles from CarMax. Additionally, CarMax owns Edmunds, a digital automotive information and shopping platform, which is not a reportable segment but is included in consolidated results.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: CarMax leverages proprietary, cloud-based digital platforms and advanced data science, including AI and machine learning, to optimize inventory management, pricing, and customer experience. The company employs an omni-channel platform that integrates online and in-store sales processes, enabling customers to buy, finance, or sell vehicles digitally or in person. Vehicle reconditioning is performed to meet CarMax Quality Certified standards, using a mix of in-house and third-party services, and all vehicles undergo a comprehensive inspection before sale.
categories.primary_customers_markets: CarMax primarily serves individual consumers seeking to buy, sell, or finance used vehicles, as well as licensed dealers who purchase vehicles through CarMax's wholesale auctions. The company targets a broad spectrum of retail customers across the credit spectrum and also provides digital appraisal and auction services to dealers. Edmunds serves both consumers and automotive dealers/OEMs with digital advertising and subscription services.
categories.geographic_coverage: As of February 28, 2023, CarMax operated 240 used car stores across 109 U.S. television markets, covering approximately 85% of the U.S. population. The company has a significant presence in the Southeastern U.S., California, Texas, and the Washington, D.C./Baltimore area. All operations are U.S.-based, with no international retail presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: CarMax operates primarily at the downstream end of the automotive supply chain, focusing on retailing and wholesaling used vehicles directly to consumers and dealers. The company sources inventory upstream from consumers, auctions, dealers, and fleet owners, and manages reconditioning and retail preparation internally or through partners.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: CarMax's strategic priorities center on enhancing its omni-channel customer experience, expanding digital capabilities, and driving operational efficiencies. Key initiatives include investment in technology to support online self-progression, finance-based shopping, logistics optimization, and digital appraisal products. The company is also focused on growing its market share, expanding its presence in electric vehicles, and leveraging data analytics to improve customer engagement and operational performance.
categories.revenue_model: CarMax generates revenue primarily through the sale of used vehicles at retail and wholesale, as well as related products and services such as extended protection plans and vehicle repair. Financing income is earned through CAF, which provides auto loans to CarMax customers. Additional revenue streams include fees from third-party finance providers, advertising and subscription revenues from Edmunds, and service department operations.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: CarMax is the largest used vehicle retailer in the U.S., with an estimated 4.0% nationwide market share of 0- to 10-year-old used vehicles. Key competitors include franchised new and used car dealers, independent used car dealers, online-focused retailers (e.g., Carvana, Vroom), and private sellers. In wholesale auctions, CarMax competes with both in-person and online auction platforms. In auto finance, CAF competes with banks, credit unions, and captive finance companies.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For fiscal year 2023, CarMax reported $29.7 billion in net sales and operating revenues, with 807,823 used vehicles sold at retail and 585,071 vehicles sold at wholesale. The company experienced a 6.9% decline in revenue and a 57.9% decrease in net earnings year-over-year, reflecting macroeconomic headwinds. CarMax targets long-term growth to 2–2.4 million vehicles sold and $33–45 billion in revenue by fiscal 2026, with a focus on profitable market share gains.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: CarMax differentiates itself through a customer-centric, no-haggle pricing model, a broad selection of quality-certified vehicles, and a flexible omni-channel buying experience. The company offers unique features such as a 30-day money-back guarantee, 24-hour test drives, and transparent, competitive financing options. Its scale, proprietary technology, and integrated digital and physical infrastructure provide customers with convenience, trust, and choice unmatched by traditional dealerships.
